title: The score
html:
Per heal: healing, effective healing (what was missing), overhealing.

Per healer:

  • Effective HPS: the healing that was needed, per second
  • Overheal %
  • Mana: healing per mana, time to OOM, mana left at the end
  • Deaths: the chance that a player in its assignment dies
  • Scares: how often a player in its assignment drops under 20% health and lives, a minute

The score (worked out 2026-11-02 by two independent agents, one from how healing is judged and simmed elsewhere, one from experiments on tools/healbench; they agree). Proposed, for the project's decisions below:

  • Primary: damage carried. The highest scale of a profile's damage at which fights end with a death in under 5% of them, found by bisection with interpolation between the two closest scales, paired seeds and about 1,600 iterations a step (about 8 sims a score). It weighs throughput against mana on its own, and it resolves a 3% gear change (+150 healing or +33 mp5 both moved the raid profile's carry from 0.666 to 0.688). It's the same shape as the tank sim's "healing needed".
  • Scored per role, since the two rank builds differently: a tank healer (one healer, the tank's damage, tank deaths) and a raid healer (raid damage, the others' deaths). In the experiments the efficient rotation won the tank role (1.17 against 0.96) and the mid-rank rotation the raid role.
  • At a set fight length, since length flips rankings: at 90 s throughput builds win, at 300 s efficient ones (raid profile: the top-rank rotation 0.80 against the efficient one's 0.71 at 90 s, 0.55 against 0.59 at 300 s).
  • Next to it: the profile's death floor (the deaths no healing stops, as the tank bench reports), mana left and time to OOM at a standard load, effective healing per mana, scares at the carry, overhealing as a diagnostic.
  • Not EHPS. At a load everyone survives, every build's EHPS is the damage taken (seven tank rotations spent 10.7k to 18.3k mana for the same 458 to 464 EHPS), and at an overload deaths cut the damage there is to heal.
  • Scares mostly echo deaths: about none at a standard load, and they show near the cliff how a build fails. Reported, not scored.
  • The comp search uses healing as a constraint, not a DPS term: a set of healers (with its tanks) qualifies when its carry at the encounter's damage is at least 1 plus a margin, for tank and raid deaths both. The healer count is the smallest that qualifies, and qualifying sets rank by raid DPS as today, so Mana Tide, Power Infusion and Innervate still count. Carry doesn't add up across healers (two healers on one tank carry far less than twice one), so sets are simmed whole: each tank's healers and the raid's healers on their own, carry tabulated per preset set, with fixed stand-in fillers.

Engine metrics the score needs (H2): per-iteration raid outcomes (anyone died, a tank died, first death, dead player-seconds; "Most deaths (one player)" undercounts the chance anyone dies, 11.4% against 14.8%), a healer's real OOM time, each healer's deaths and scares within its assignment, effective healing per mana, a profile's death floor, and heals in flight so healers stop sniping each other.

H1: what's in (2026-11-02)

  • Overhealing. Every heal books the part that found its target at full health (TargetedActionMetrics.overhealing, sim/core/spell_result.go), and each unit has an effective HPS (UnitMetrics.ehps: healing less overhealing, no shielding) next to HPS. A target dummy has no health bar, so a heal on it is all effective. The healing table has an Overheal column.
  • The healing fight (Encounter.track_health). Every player loses health to every hit it takes and dies when it runs out (sim/core/player_death.go): its cast stops, its rotation, swings and auras end, the mobs on it turn to the next living tank (or any living player once no tank is left), heals don't reach it and nothing it would cast goes. Its pets and dots carry on. A fight without the switch is unchanged, so the DPS Report's numbers didn't move.
  • Scares (UnitMetrics.scares_avg): a dip under 20% health that we live through, counted once until we're back over 50%, per fight. A dip that ends in death is a death, not a scare.
  • Raid damage events (Encounter.raid_damage, sim/core/raid_damage.go): school, damage range, who (everyone, the tanks, the others, or the boss's target, all of them or N random), timing (every N ± a spread, or random with an average) and an optional DoT. Physical goes through armor, the rest through resistances.
  • Tank swaps (Target.tank_swap_seconds): the boss turns to the next living tank on a timer. Each iteration starts on the first tank again.
  • Heal targets in the rotation: Most Hurt, Lowest Health and Tank N (UnitReference), the Health Missing value, and Max Health on any unit. Health % of Most Hurt or Lowest Health reads 100% when nobody is hurt, and a heal at them waits. The APL editor offers them, and every player, as cast targets.
  • Assignments (Player.heal_assignment): the players and tanks a healer's Most Hurt and Lowest Health pick from. Proto only for now; the raid sim fills it in H6.
  • The shaman's heals land on the player they're cast at, and on the shaman for a cast at a mob, so the leveling sim is unchanged. Chain Heal jumps to the 2 most hurt (within the target's party when it's in ours), each jump 50% of the one before. Riptide can go on anyone.
  • Tests: sim/raid_healing_test.go (heals on others and overhealing, death stopping a player, tank swaps).

title: The bench and the roles
html:
The engine books how a healing fight went (RaidMetrics.healing_fight): fights, fights with any death, a tank's death and another's, the first death's time and the seconds players spent dead, as counts and sums so results combine. Each unit has its mana spent a fight (UnitMetrics.mana_spent_avg), for effective healing per mana. A healer that wants a heal it can't pay for is marked out of mana by the engine as any caster is; the "time to OOM wrong" finding was the dead healers' regen, fixed with the audit.

tools/healbench scores by role (-role tank|raid|both), against a made-up -profile or a boss from tools/encounters (-encounter, at the boss's own fight length):

  • tank: the boss's melee and its abilities on the tanks, one healer by default, assigned the tanks; fails when a tank dies in 2% of fights.
  • raid: the damage on the raid only, no tanks; fails when anyone dies in 5%.
  • both: everything; either line fails.

-carry finds the damage carried (the scale of all damage at the line: bracketed, bisected five times on the same seed, interpolated) and the death floor there (every player topped off every 1.5 ± 0.5 s, so only a one-shot or a burst between heals kills; -floor prints it at -scale). About 10 sims, 2.5 s for a tank role score at 800 iterations.

title: Damage
html:
The boss's melee on its tank, as today. A boss can have its own tank, and an encounter can swap tanks on a timer or on a debuff's stacks, so a two-tank fight has both tanks taking hits in turn.

Raid damage events, a list on the encounter. Each one is an ability of the boss:

  • its school and its damage range, before the player's resistances and damage taken modifiers
  • when: every N seconds with a spread, or at random times with an average rate, from a start time
  • who: every player, N random players, the tanks, the melee, or the players in one group (a cleave, a breath, a bolt volley on the nearest)
  • once or over time (a DoT on its targets)

The DPS Report's raid damage hits stay as they are: a DPS sim doesn't heal, so they take no health there.

Damage profiles are named sets of those settings. They come from Classic and Season of Discovery bosses whose numbers are on record, picked to cover the shapes healers meet:

ShapeStand-inWhat it tests
One tank, steadyPatchwerk: heavy melee, Hateful Strike on the healthiest melee in reachtank healing, the off-tanks' spikes
Two tanks, swappingBroodlord Lashlayer or Ragnaros: a knockback that hands the boss to the second tankhealing two tanks, switching targets
Raid damageVaelastrasz or Sapphiron: steady damage on everyoneraid heals, mana over a long fight
Spiky random targetsOnyxia: Fireball on random members, Deep Breath, a phase of raid damage. Onyxia's Lair is one of Forever's launch raids, so Forever's own numbers replace Classic's when they're known.reaction, scares
A 10-player raidSeason of Discovery's Blackfathom Deeps (Aku'mai or Kelris)the small raid, two healers

The numbers come from Warcraft Logs, which shows what Blizzard's servers did (the project, 2026-11-02): Season of Discovery logs first, then Anniversary (Vanilla, then TBC), then Era, with vmangos only as a last resort where no log shows a value (data_sources.md, Which source wins). Each profile names its reports. The logs also show how real raids healed each boss: healer counts, HPS and overhealing, which the sim's healers can be checked against. Forever's raids are 10, 20 and 40 players, so each profile scales its damage to the raid. When Forever's bosses are known, each gets its own profile.

title: Raid damage from the logs
html:
The seven boss files (tools/encounters, shared with the tank sim) have their raid side from Warcraft Logs: the boss's damage on the players who aren't tanks as raidDamage events with who NotTanks, and what real raids had in raidHealing. The tank sim scores on the Anniversary realms' set (tools/encounters/*.json, the project's ruling to the tank session), so that's the one benched here; Season of Discovery's is in tools/encounters/sod/. How they're mined and written: tools/warcraftlogs/wclcli.py raid (wclraid.py) and tools/encounters/raid_from_logs.py, README in both folders.

  • The tanks in a log are the players the bosses swung at (5% or more of the swings) and the players who tanked an add (30% or more of its swings: Golemagg's two Core Rager tanks, Broodlord's whelps). The rest are the non-tanks, and their damage taken is the raid side. The players' own damage (runes, sapper charges, Hellfire, Seal of Martyrdom) is left out.
  • An event is an ability with 2% or more of the non-tanks' damage in 10% or more of the kills: its unmitigated hit, the share of the non-tanks a cast hits (the new RaidDamageEvent.share, so the file fits a 10, 20 or 40 player raid), a DoT's ticks, and the rate that lands the logs' damage a second on each non-tank after its first cast. Every file's events land what the logs did, within 0.1 a second.
  • healbench -role raid and both run the logs' median kill (Onyxia 137 s, Chromaggus 115 s), since the file's duration is the main tank's time on the boss.

  • both doesn't compare with the logs as it stands. The tank's damage doesn't shrink with the raid: a 10-player bench raid puts 2 or 3 healers on a tank that 40-player raids gave 6 to 8 (the tank session's healing.healers). Ragnaros and Vaelastrasz kill the tank whatever the raid healers do. The check against the logs is per role: tank at the file's tank healers, raid at the logs' raid healers a non-tank.
  • raid carries 1 or more on four bosses, as the logs' deathless kills say it should. Onyxia, Broodlord and Chromaggus fall short with mana to spare (6,458, 7,145 and 7,441 left), so it's spikes, not throughput: Broodlord's Blast Wave (2,678 to 3,336 Fire on half the raid at once), Onyxia's Flame Breath and Fireballs on a Frost mage's health. A 40-player raid answers a spike with any of its 11 healers; the bench's 2 at the same ratio react slower. The death floor is under 2% on all three, so a heal could have saved them.
  • Not yet in the files: the logs' cast timing and phases (each event is at random times after its first cast), players' fire resistance gear and self-saves (the logs' damage is after them; the sim's mages take it unmitigated by gear), and who stands where (each cast hits random non-tanks).

title: Who heals whom
html:
Each healer has an assignment: a set of players it heals, which the rotation's smart targets choose from. An assignment is one or more tanks, a group, or the raid. With none, it's the whole raid.

New targets for the rotation (UnitReference types):

  • Most hurt: the player in the assignment missing the most health (for a big heal)
  • Lowest health: the lowest health percent in the assignment (for a fast heal)
  • Tank N: the raid's Nth tank
  • each of them only among living players, and none when nobody is hurt, so a heal on it waits

With these, an APL reads "Flash Heal on Lowest health when it's under 50%" or "Renew on Tank 1 when it's missing". New values go with them: a unit's health missing, and its max health.

Several healers on the same target: in the game, a healer sees the other healers' casts, and in the sim two healers can both start a big heal on the same tank, and one heal lands as overheal. That's real, it's overhealing. A first version doesn't model healers watching each other's casts, and the overheal it causes is part of the score.

Chain Heal jumps to the most hurt players, within the target's party when it's in ours (the tooltip). The group heals (Prayer of Healing, Tranquility, Holy Nova, Healing Stream, Light's Vigil's party heal) reach a party and don't jump. Everyone is in reach of everyone for now (the raid sim's ruling for buffs), which flatters Chain Heal's jumps between melee and ranged.

title: Rulings
html:
• What a healer is scored on: effective healing per second, efficient use of mana, keeping the tanks and the raid alive, and as few "scares" as possible (a tank or member brought close to death who lives).
  • How heals pick targets: assignments plus smart targets in the rotation. Each healer has an assignment (a tank, several tanks, or the raid), and the rotation can aim a heal at "the most hurt in my assignment" and similar. The raid sim fills assignments on its own, and the project can set any of them by hand.
  • Who takes damage: the main tank, several tanks in some encounters, and per encounter other raid members (the project: "Healers need to simulate main tanks (or multiple tanks in certain encounters) and sometimes various other raid members taking damage (depending on encounter)").
  • The damage until Forever's bosses exist (no boss data before 2026-12-09): configurable damage profiles, with some representative Classic and Season of Discovery bosses as stand-ins.
  • The score (2026-11-02, after the scoring agents' report): damage carried, the highest scale of a profile's damage the healers hold, with separate lines: tank deaths in under 2% of fights, the others' deaths in under 5%. Judged at the encounter's own fight length. **Separate tank healer and raid healer scores per build, and presets per role. In the raid sim healing is a requirement with a 20% margin** (healers carry 1.2 times the encounter's damage), checked against Warcraft Logs: the healer counts, healing and deaths real raids had on each boss.
  • Downranking (2026-11-02): no action that picks the exact rank out of all of a heal's ranks. Players bind 2 to 4 ranks of a heal and choose one of those by the situation, so a rotation does the same: it casts at most 4 ranks of a heal, each on its own condition.
  • Order: the shared groundwork now. Nobody else is building it (the tank session stopped after its tank sheet and bench, waiting on its own open decisions).

title: The mean
html: A healer's score is its damage carried (healbench -carry), 1,000 iterations a sim at each boss file's own length, on the bench's seed (101). Its mean is over the seven boss files, Ragnaros included, as the healing docs average them; tank healers (one healer, the tank's damage, fails at 2% tank deaths) and raid healers (the raid's damage, fails at 5% deaths) are ranked apart.
